Hi, Light! I’d like to share my impressions after reading the first arc.

I have no words to express how I feel after finishing it, only feelings remain. My only regret is that I didn’t read all the character stories before the final chapter. But I suppose I would have cried even harder in that case. Even if it’s not without flaws, it’s a very beautiful story with an equally beautiful ending. For the first time, it was hard for me to say something about the characters, since their main development remains outside the main plot. And I only truly fell in love with the protagonist of this story right at the very end.

I don’t yet know how to put all these emotions and impressions on paper. Usually I can say a lot, but here there’s not even anything to say. It’s simply... an amazing story.

What’s also sad is that the company didn’t have the opportunity to finish the first arc the way you wanted to. And yet the finale was very sad, especially against the backdrop of the history of what was happening at that time.

Thanks to the team for giving us such a wonderful story. I hope that one day you’ll have a chance to show the first arc the way it was originally meant to be.

无论哪个版本，都是我们辛苦设计的结果。很感谢有守密人更喜欢早期的设计。不管哪一边，我们想创造的都是「易于上手、难于精通」的体验，也一直在努力维护和创造那种真正有效的决策差异。

但国际服的平衡设计，你看到的可以说是千疮百孔。原因在于，当时我们没有看到这个游戏未来会怎样扩展和变化，于是不断修改，补上了两三屏都看不完的补充平衡规则。每一次平衡失衡，都会把许多原本细心打磨过的体验破坏掉。回头看，国际服早期的设计里有相当多的矛盾：有些选择看起来存在，其实是假的；有些效果噪音很多，花了很多精力去理解，玩下来却没有实际作用。

日服的设计更保守，但仍然建立在同样的「意义感」上。比如熔毁·朵尔的「缸中之脑」能力，就是国际服里我们没来得及深挖的主题；杜勒赛因我们也会融入「吞噬即获得记忆」的主题。效果保守的好处是，像星辰篇就几乎没有负面限制类的平衡规则，精力可以聚焦在那些真正有意义的选择上。

我们会吸取两边实践的经验，让各自的设计继续进化。

Whichever version it is, both are the result of hard design work. I'm grateful that some Keepers prefer the earlier design. On either side, what we want to create is an experience that's easy to pick up but hard to master, and we've kept working to preserve and create decisions that genuinely matter.

But the balance design of the global server, as you've seen, is riddled with holes. The reason is that back then we couldn't see how the game would expand and change, so we kept patching it, adding supplementary balance rules that run two or three screens long. Every time the balance broke, it destroyed a lot of carefully polished experiences along with it. Looking back, the early global design had plenty of contradictions: some choices only looked like choices, and some effects were so noisy that they took real effort to understand yet made little actual difference in play.

The JP design is more conservative, but it's built on the same sense of meaning. Doll: Inferno's "Brain in a Vat" ability, for instance, is a theme we never had the chance to dig into on global; and for Doresain we'll be weaving in the theme of "devour to gain memories." The upside of conservative effects is that Astral Reign, for example, has almost no negative-restriction balance rules, so the attention can go to the choices that genuinely matter.

We'll take the lessons from both runs and let each design keep evolving.

I think this is an opinion shared by many long-time players who have already stopped playing, but the recent (last 6 months) game direction has been pulling Morimens away from the game that we fell in love with in Arc1.

The devs' priorities and wishes for how the game functions are at odds with the playerbase's, and nothing makes it more apparent than being able to see JP vs Global.

The new realm units and relics are closer in line with JP, because as Light has stated: JP is how he *wishes* Morimens was like on release. Yet you can pluck pretty much anyone who has an informed opinion on the server and they would tell you they find JP odd/different at best and a cashgrabby stain they would never touch at worst.

What playerbase are you even appealing to anymore? The newer units are skewed for general appeal, with kits that are easy to plug and play to great efficacy. But the fanbase you originally got off the ground with liked the interplay and subtle complexity between units. People who play cardgames *generally* like nuance. People who like roguelites like StS *generally* like games that demand skill. Heavier RNG-reliance, enemies(and to a lesser degree even some playable cards that further push powercreep) that have huge wall of numbers, effects that lack countermeasures to respond with-- these are not nuanced or skill-based. These are not fun.

I understand the need for wider appeal, but I can't help but feel completely alienated from the design choices as of late-- from both a story and gameplay angle.

这里有一个结构性的原因：大家的作战实力、护盾和回复能力会随着强度提高而提高，但血量上限和护盾上限不会。于是，一个「合理的挑战」里，敌人的伤害相对于血量会越来越高。这很反直觉，但数学上是成立的。即便在这么严苛的情况下，有些生存向队伍配合回血能力，仍然能活到四五十回合和敌人打持久战。

如果不这么严苛，挑战感就不强，比较随便就能堆够生存。

这是游戏后期环境在数学结构上的问题，我们需要小心地寻找办法。

There's a structural reason behind this: your combat power, Shield, and healing all scale up as strength increases, but the HP cap and Shield cap do not. So in any "reasonable challenge," enemy damage relative to your HP keeps climbing. It's counterintuitive, but the math holds. Even under conditions this harsh, some survival-oriented teams with healing can still last forty or fifty turns in a war of attrition against the enemy.

If it weren't this harsh, there'd be little sense of challenge; survivability would be easy to stack without much thought.

This is a mathematical, structural issue in the game's late-game environment, and we need to look for solutions carefully.

Enemies can no longer inflict meaningful damage, players spend turn after turn accomplishing nothing, and they can freely exploit recovery mechanics to completely bypass the risks the developers originally intended.

I understand exactly why you would want to prevent such situations. However, that does not justify making all forms of defense meaningless. Mindless, thoughtless defensive strategies should absolutely be subject to the design philosophy described above. As someone who has encountered similar design problems many times, I agree with that principle. But when a defensive strategy is backed by sufficient character investment, counterpicks against enemy strategies, and a deep understanding of both the player's and the enemy's combat patterns, defense should be allowed to succeed. At that point, the supposedly "meaningless turns" are no longer meaningless at all. They represent both the opportunity cost the player willingly accepted by choosing a defensive strategy and the reward they earned through investment, knowledge, and careful planning.

During this game's earliest tests, most people complained about the difficulty, but we held to it as our distinctive flavor. When we added the D-Effect Zone, many were against it too, and it genuinely put challenge pressure on everyone. When we introduced the Astral Reign rules to recalibrate the balance environment, we took a serious beating for it. But we still had to do it. Keepers who understand the state of the game's balance know that without that chapter, continuing within the Faded Legacy framework might have killed the game long ago and made it impossible to maintain.

That doesn't mean every decision we've made was right. There have been plenty of times we messed up. But some major design directions genuinely can't be settled by a vote. Valuing everyone's voice and feedback, and deciding how the game should improve and solve its problems, are actually two different things. We care deeply about both. What we can do is keep learning from our mistakes, so that our odds of judging correctly keep rising, and keep finding ways to repair the problems of the past.

Please re-evaluate your actual target audience. Not the people hanging out in Discord, but the people who are actually playing the game.

Right now, your team is trying to straddle the fence, attempting to strike a balance between casual players and those interested in challenging content. In doing so, however, you end up alienating both sides. When changes are made to cater to casual players, hardcore players become frustrated because the game feels too easy; they lose interest and gradually leave as such changes continue.

The same applies in reverse. When you frequently shift focus, a segment of the player base decides to quit because the game’s direction keeps oscillating between different priorities.

In gacha games, the endgame should always be designed for hardcore players. It is their playground, the part of the game they find most engaging. By simplifying it, you frustrate these players and, consequently, lose out on potential revenue.

Story-driven content, on the other hand, is naturally aimed at casual players. For them, there are other modes, such as the Hectic Skybound Train, P-Dive, and Traphase to enjoy.

Remember that yours is a gacha game. Your goal should be to encourage players to spend money, rather than having them simply remain content with what they already have. Challenging content drives players to pull for characters, and when they run out of pulls, it creates an incentive to spend.

Casual players are not the primary target audience for gacha games. Please keep this in mind when making balancing decisions.

If you find it difficult to balance the game across different modes, consider implementing mode-specific effects that apply only within those particular areas. For example, you can upgrade cards for Train only, but they will remain as they are in P-Dive or D-Zone.

谢谢你。关于这个 bug 的情况，我来说明一下。你举的中毒例子，触发的是敌人身上的「中毒」状态，这是一个作用在敌人身上的效果。而唤醒体的能力，绝大部分需要唤醒体自身的行动才能生效，并不是自带一个全队都能触发的造物。除非特别说明，基本都需要这样理解。皮克曼这个根据我们目前的记录是以前也不能触发，也可能在本地化方面有时候会有一些错误。这些错误修正可能造成大家的误解。
过往我们在 bug 的发现和处理公布上，确实有做得不够好的地方，也确实有非常多的 bug，这是我们在持续努力改进的地方。很抱歉这些修正让你感到不公平。我们绝不会为了削弱而进行修正，只会为了让规则明确而修正。
关于回溯，每一个案例我们都会核实这次调整是否影响了大家当初的投入判断。例如卡斯托尔的机制调整，绝大多数情况下是增强，所以我们没有提供回溯；而有些命轮的补偿幅度可能不够，所以后来复审时开放了回溯。
Thank you. Let me explain the situation with this bug. The Poison examples you cited trigger off the "Poison" state on the enemy, which is an effect applied to the enemy. Awakener abilities, on the other hand, almost always require the Awakener's own action to take effect. They are not built-in team-wide triggers. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, that is how they should be read. As for Pickman, according to our current records this could not be triggered by others before either. There may also have been localization errors at times, and correcting those errors may have led to misunderstandings.
In the past we have indeed fallen short in how we found bugs and announced their fixes, and there have truly been a great many bugs. This is something we keep working to improve. I'm sorry these fixes made you feel treated unfairly. We never make a fix in order to nerf. We only fix to make the rules clear.
As for refunds, in every case we check whether the adjustment affected the judgment players made when they invested. For example, Castor's mechanic adjustment was a buff in the vast majority of situations, so we offered no refund. For some Wheels of Destiny, the compensation may not have been enough, so a later review opened a refund.

Hi Light, what I’m going to say isn’t directly related to Morimens or your job as its producer, but it might as well be.
I want to advise you to care about Morimens a little less—not more, but less. Paradoxically, sitting back a bit might actually help you make the game better.
We’ve all seen you pulling all-nighters and staying up until dawn replying to player feedback. Everyone agrees you’re deeply passionate, but there is only so much one person can accomplish in a short time. Sometimes, rushing to change things on a whim only to rush into more changes when people complain does far more damage than holding steady. Some decisions simply need to be sat out.
Staying up late constantly damages your body and your prefrontal cortex, making you far more prone to rushed, emotional decisions you’ll regret later. Beyond that, taking the frontline community role every day blurs the line between criticism of the game and personal attacks directed at you. It creates an unhealthy parasocial cycle of love, hate, and resentment with the community, esp veteran CN players (they’re also super passionate about the game and their opinions).

Constant engagement also leaves players frustrated when you repeatedly acknowledge their complaints without having the immediate capacity to fix them.
Please force yourself to sleep well, get up earlier, and let your live ops colleagues handle player engagement when you’re exhausted. Passion is wonderful, but don't let Morimens consume your entire life. Maintaining your mental health is vital if you want to keep going for the long haul.

Hi Light，我要说的虽然不直接关于《忘却前夜》或者你作为制作人的具体工作，但其实也息息相关。
我想劝你对《忘却前夜》少上心一点。不是更多，而是少一点。稍微往后退一步，或许反而能帮你把这款游戏做得更好。
大家都看得到你经常熬夜。没人会怀疑你的热情，但一个人在短时间内能做到的事情终究有限。有时候，一时冲动急着去改动，等有人抱怨了又急着再改，反而比维持现状带来的伤害更大。
长期熬夜会损害身体和大脑的前额叶皮层，让你更容易做出冲动、情绪化的决定，事后又陷入后悔。此外，每天冲在社区第一线，会模糊玩家对游戏的批评与对你个人的攻击之间的界限，进而与同样对游戏抱有极高热情的CN老玩家们——陷入互相伤害中。
而且，这种频频回应，却无法解决问题的状态，只会让玩家在一次次得到确认却看不到改变时感到更加失望。
好好睡觉、早点起床吧。把玩家沟通的工作多交给同事们去处理。作为游戏开发者，照顾好自己的心理健康，才是走得更远的关键。
